response:
Looking at this carefully against all 46 prior findings. Tracing execution paths, checking interactions between the six Run 10 fixes and existing logic.

---

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`: when `_apply_transform()` returns `None` (parameter already at its target value — a no-op), no `set_remediation_state()` is called, no adjustment is recorded, and `chain_idx` never advances. On the next round the same pathology fires, `apply_diagnosis` reads `state = self.health_monitor._remediation_state.get(chain_key, {})` → empty → `chain_idx = 0` → same no-op transform → infinite loop. No escalation, no exhaustion recorded. Combined with the Run 10 `tau_sim` default change from 0.8 to 0.33: `lower_tau_sim_01` moves tau_sim from 0.33 to `max(0.3, 0.23)` = 0.3 on first application (works once). On recurrence, step 0 is `max(0.3, 0.3-0.1) = 0.3` (no-op), step 1 same, step 2 `lower_tau_sim_to_floor` sets to 0.3 (no-op). The entire `kappa_stuck` chain is permanently stalled after one successful application — all three steps are no-ops, but the chain never registers exhaustion because `_apply_transform` returns `None` and `apply_diagnosis` silently exits.
PROPOSED_FIX: When `_apply_transform` returns `None`, check whether the parameter is already at the chain step's target value. If so, advance `chain_idx` in `_remediation_state` to skip the no-op step, or record chain exhaustion if no further steps exist. Additionally, adjust the `kappa_stuck` chain floor from 0.3 to a value below the new default (e.g., 0.15) to restore meaningful remediation range.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`: the vocab_growth improvement check reads `tau_vg = self._config.tau_vocab_growth` at verification time, but the `halve_tau_vocab` transform already modified this value when the remediation was applied. Trace: round R detects vocab_saturation, applies `halve_tau_vocab` (tau_vg 0.04 → 0.02), records `metric_at_apply = 0.03`. Round R+2 verifies: `current_val = 0.03`, `improved = 0.03 >= 0.02` → True. Remediation declared SUCCESSFUL even though vocab_growth didn't change — the threshold moved, not the metric. This self-fulfilling verification contaminates `_step_effectiveness` tracking (inflating success count for `halve_tau_vocab`) and `remediation_success_rate`, which in turn suppresses self-check 1 in `self_diagnose()`.
PROPOSED_FIX: Snapshot the relevant threshold at application time (store `tau_vg_at_apply` alongside `metric_at_apply` in remediation state). At verification time, compare `current_val >= tau_vg_at_apply` (the original threshold), not the modified one. Apply the same principle to any remediation that modifies the metric's own detection threshold (tau_sim for kappa, etc.).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.87
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `process_round()`, F005 fix block: the `_regression_defer` reset logic checks `self._pre_fix_snapshots` for ongoing regressions, but runs AFTER the snapshot cleanup that removes all snapshots where `round_idx - s["round"] >= 2`. The reset check filters for `round_idx - s["round"] >= 2` — exactly the snapshots already removed. So `regression_this_round` is always `False`, `_healthy_rounds_since_regression` always increments, and `_regression_defer` unconditionally resets after `resolution_hysteresis` rounds (default 2). The F005 fix intended to prevent permanent autonomous remediation blocking, but it makes the regression-defer mechanism effectively a 2-round pause regardless of whether a regression is actually ongoing.
PROPOSED_FIX: Move the F005 reset check BEFORE the snapshot cleanup. Or capture the regression check result during the main regression detection loop and reuse it in the reset logic instead of re-scanning the already-pruned snapshot list.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: `bench/immune_agents.py`, `_verify_z3()`: the if/then branch creates two unconstrained z3 Boolean variables `X` and `Y`, asserts `X` (True) and `Not(Y)` (False), then checks satisfiability. This is trivially SAT — `{X=True, Y=False}` is always a valid model. The variables are never connected to the actual claim content extracted by the regex. Every if/then logical claim is therefore REJECTED with verdict `SATISFIABLE_COUNTEREXAMPLE` regardless of its truth value. The Run 10 fix note mentions f-string escaping fixes in `_verify_z3()`, but this structural logic error predates the f-string fix: the z3 solver is solving a vacuous problem.
PROPOSED_FIX: Parse the actual if/then content from the regex capture groups and encode them as z3 constraints. At minimum, if semantic parsing fails, return UNCERTAIN instead of a vacuously-derived REJECTED. The current implementation is worse than no verification because it actively produces false rejections.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `self_diagnose()`, self-check 3 (chain exhaustion rate): unlike self-checks 1 and 2, this check never writes to `_last_self_adjust_round[_trigger_key_3]` because it only emits a DEFER diagnosis without performing a self-adjustment. The damping gate reads `_last_3 = self._last_self_adjust_round.get(_trigger_key_3, -999)`, which is permanently -999. So `current_round - (-999) >= damping_rounds` is always True. Once `chain_exhaustion_rate > 0.5` and `len(self._chain_exhaustion_history) >= 2`, this CRITICAL diagnosis is emitted every single round for the rest of the experiment, flooding the diagnosis log and the event stream. With 20+ rounds this produces 15+ identical CRITICAL diagnoses.
PROPOSED_FIX: Write `self._last_self_adjust_round[_trigger_key_3] = current_round` after emitting the diagnosis, even though no self-adjustment was applied. The damping interval then prevents repeat emission until the next evaluation window.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_manager.py` + `bench/dm/_failure_handler.py`: the `no_exclusion_mode` flag (added in Run 10) only gates the `ABORT → critical_failure → FSM TERMINAL` path in `process_round()`. It does NOT gate `RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE` in `FailureHandler.get_recovery()`, which still calls `self._active_models.discard(model_id)`. Additionally, the `DOWNGRADE_ROLE` escalation for PAR models (Run 6 bug 6 fix) also calls `self._active_models.discard(model_id)`. In no_exclusion_mode, models are still removed from the active set via these paths. If enough models are excluded, `should_abort()` returns True but is suppressed by no_exclusion_mode, and eventually `get_allocation()` raises `RuntimeError("No active models available")` — an unhandled crash. The mode's name and documentation suggest models should not be excluded, but only the FSM terminal transition is protected.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `get_recovery()`, check `self.config.no_exclusion_mode` before executing EXCLUDE (demote to RETRY or LOG_ONLY instead). Similarly gate the PAR→EXCLUDE escalation. Alternatively, rename the flag to `no_abort_mode` to accurately reflect its scope.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `apply_diagnosis()`: when P-pass rejects a remediation (`proceed=False`), the code creates or updates `self.health_monitor._remediation_state[chain_key]` with `chain_idx + 1` and sets `applied_round = round_idx`, `metric_at_apply = current_metric_val`. But no fix was actually applied. After `verification_window` rounds, `_verify_remediation_outcomes` evaluates this phantom state and records an outcome — if the metric happened to improve naturally, it's logged as a successful remediation for `chain_idx + 1`. This contaminates `_step_effectiveness` (crediting a step that was never applied), `remediation_success_rate`, and `recommended_chain_start` (which may skip genuinely useful steps based on phantom success data). The phantom state also lacks `chain_length` (defaults to 999 via `.get()`), disabling the chain-exhaustion bounds check.
PROPOSED_FIX: Do not create remediation_state when P-pass rejects. Instead, record the rejection in a separate tracking structure (e.g., `_rejected_remediations`) so the chain can advance on the next diagnosis without contaminating outcome verification. The chain_length issue (ChatGPT_IM_F002 R2) should also be fixed in this path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_manager.py` and `bench/dm/_convergence.py` both define identical copies of `_finding_similarity()`, `_tokenize_for_similarity()`, `_bigrams()`, and `_STOPWORDS`. `bench/immune_agents.py` imports `_finding_similarity` from `_convergence.py` (line: `from bench.dm._convergence import _finding_similarity`), while `DynamicManager.__init__` passes `_finding_similarity` from `_manager.py` to `ConvergenceDetector`. NK Cell dedup and convergence detection use separate copies of the same function. A bug fix applied to one copy but not the other would cause silent divergence: findings classified as duplicates by the convergence detector might not be classified as duplicates by the immune pipeline, or vice versa. The tau_sim recalibration in Run 10 affects both equally only because both copies are currently identical.
PROPOSED_FIX: Delete the copy in `_manager.py` and import from `_convergence.py` (or extract to a shared `_similarity.py` module). Single source of truth for the similarity function.
VERIFIED: TRUE
